items.title: Realistic positional balance and CPU roster building
items.stageRationale: FB beta hardening: closes a demonstrated player-facing or readiness gap before public beta.
items.recipe: Measured first (see measurement). Diagnose which of progression, draft intake and retirement drives the rise in 85+ players at quarterback and tight end, then fix that cause; add surplus penalties to CPU draft, free agency and trade value so stars do not pile up in one room; gate per-position elite composition and same-position stacking with negative controls.
items.acceptance: Probe on the same seeds and windows before and after; new gates fail on the pre-fix engine and pass after; talent-distribution, progression-parity and decade tests pass.
items.premise: CPU trade value ignores position surplus

premises.claim: CPU trade value ignores position surplus
No balance probe existed before this audit

L1.recipe: Smallest player-visible slice of the recipe.

L2.recipe: Measured first (see measurement). Diagnose which of progression, draft intake and retirement drives the rise in 85+ players at quarterback and tight end, then fix that cause; add surplus penalties to CPU draft, free agency and trade value so stars do not pile up in one room; gate per-position elite composition and same-position stacking with negative controls.

L3.recipe: Full depth including the optional extensions named in the approved plan.

measurement.population: active-roster players on a club; practice squad excluded
measurement.window: seasons 0, 3, 6 and 10 on the canonical session path
measurement.finding: League creation does not stack a position: no club starts with two 85+ quarterbacks. The defect arrives with time. By season 6, and holding through season 10, the number of 85+ quarterbacks is two to four times the starting count, up to four clubs hold two or more, and one club holds three. Tight ends, offensive linemen, linebackers and defensive backs inflate as well. The cause is therefore growth in elite count over seasons (progression and intake) with stacking as its consequence, not creation-time distribution.
measurement.limits: Three seeds and ten seasons. Counts level off between seasons 6 and 10, which suggests a raised steady state rather than unbounded growth; a season-20 reading would confirm it. No per-position real-football baseline has been set for these counts yet.
